If you haven’t yet, order some body armor.

You spend hundreds a month on various insurance that you won’t need. Think of this as insurance against the inevitable (chaos is coming, regardless of how much we wish it away).

Level 3 or higher is what you want. This means nice thin (but heavy) metal plates or super thick composite plates (which are gay and also fail faster). You can purchase a plate carrier with level 3 plates for under $300.

Some companies offer “level 3+”, which does in fact provide more protection against some fairly common rounds (like M855 green tip .556 rounds) while not being nearly as heavy as level 4 (level 4 is unbearably heavy).

Here’s a great set for $277 (w/ level 3+ selected):

https://www.ar500armor.com/plate-carriers/plate-carrier-packages-w-armor/veritas-general-issue-package-new.html

Plan on waiting many weeks for your order (for obv reasons). There are many other stores selling AR 500 armor as well, but I think the leadtimes are fairly similar across-the-board.

You’ll find many level 3A soft armor vests, but level 3A won’t even really slow down a rifle round. In fact, you can watch videos on YouTube of people shooting through 2 layers or more of level 3A like butter with a .556 and M93 or M855. It only protects against pistol rounds. However, you can purchase a level 3A vest that also accepts plates. Adding level 3+ plates to a level 3A vest makes it effectively level 4. Another added benefit of this approach is that the vest collects the spalling (lead splatter) that will otherwise spread out to your face and arms when you’re hit. While spalling is less dangerous than a direct hit, it’ll still ruin your day.

Here’s an option for that:

https://bulletsafe.com/products/the-bulletsafe-level-iiia-tactical-bulletproof-vest-kit

This vest in particular does not do as well as some of the higher end soft vests out there at repeated hits in the same spot (e.g., reuse in a protracted battle), but it offers way better wrap around protection and also acts as a plate carrier.
